what.a: A contract that tracks an asset’s price without ever expiring. You never own the coin — you hold a position that gains or loses as the price moves, and you can bet on it falling as easily as rising.

funding.a: Because the contract never expires, something has to keep its price tied to the real one. Every few hours, whichever side is crowded pays the other. Hold a popular long position for a week and funding alone can cost more than the move you were waiting for.

liquidation.a: Your position is backed by collateral. When losses eat that collateral, the venue closes the position and the collateral is gone — you do not get a margin call and a chance to top up. The table below shows how small that move is.

leverage.a: It multiplies both directions equally. At 100x a 1% move in your favour doubles your money and a 1% move against you leaves nothing. Crypto routinely moves 1% in minutes, so at high leverage the question is not whether you are right about direction but whether you are right before noise stops you out.

costs.q: What does it cost to hold?
costs.a: Three things, all continuous: the trading fee when you open and close, funding every few hours, and the spread. A position held for weeks can bleed away even if the price ends exactly where it started.

perp.fundingTitle: What it costs to hold, by venue
perp.fundingIntro: Funding is the fee perpetual traders pay each other every few hours to keep the contract tied to the spot price. It is charged whether your trade is winning or losing, and the same position costs a different amount at every venue. Rates below are live and annualised so they can be compared.
perp.fundSpread: The gap between the cheapest and dearest venue for {{symbol}} is {{spread}} percentage points a year, on an identical position.

crowd.shorts: Shorts are crowded on {{symbol}} — sellers are paying buyers, currently about {{apr}} a year.

perp.costTitle: What holding it would cost you
perp.costExplain: That is {{pct}}% of the money you put in, for one month, before the price moves at all. Leverage multiplies this cost exactly as fast as it multiplies a gain — at {{lev}}× you pay funding on {{lev}}× your collateral.

perp.thirdPartyNoticeEarning: These are independent third-party protocols. Fanous Bazaar Pishgam is not the counterparty, does not control them, and cannot help recover losses. We do receive a share of the trading fee from GMX when you use our link — and you receive a 5% fee discount for the same reason, so the link costs you less than going direct. Verify every URL yourself — perp venues are a common phishing target.

how.title: How do perpetual futures work?
how.p1: A perpetual future is a contract that tracks an asset’s price without ever expiring. You are not buying the coin — you are taking a position on where its price goes, and you can do that in either direction.
how.p2: Leverage means the exchange lends you exposure. At 10x, $100 of your own money controls $1,000 of position. A 10% move in your favour doubles your money; a 10% move against you erases it entirely. That second sentence is the one that matters and it is why most accounts using high leverage end at zero.
how.p3: Because the contract never expires, a "funding rate" keeps its price tied to the real market. Every few hours, whichever side is crowded pays the other. Hold a position long enough and funding alone can cost more than the price move you were right about.
how.p4: Liquidation is automatic. If the market moves far enough against you, the position closes and the money is gone — there is no margin call and nobody to appeal to.

farm.subtitle: Live yields from across DeFi, filtered down to pools large enough and old enough to be worth your time.
farm.whatBody: You deposit into a pool and earn a share of what it makes: interest from borrowers, a cut of every swap, or rewards for helping secure a network. All of it is paid by someone doing something real — which is why a pool advertising 900% a year is not paying you out of revenue.
farm.ilBody: If the two tokens move apart in price, you end up holding more of the loser and less of the winner — possibly worse off than just holding them, even after fees. The wider the gap, the worse it gets. Stablecoin pairs barely suffer; volatile pairs suffer a lot.

farm.custodyNotice: These pools are run by their own protocols, not by Fanous Bazaar Pishgam. You deposit directly from your own wallet into their contracts — we never touch your funds and we take no cut of your yield. If you use our swap to get the tokens first, that swap pays our normal {{fee}}% fee and nothing else does.

farm.stakingIntro: Swap into one of these and you are staking. There is no deposit to make, nothing to lock, and no impermanent loss — the token's value against SOL grows every few days, and swapping back out is how you stop. You keep it in your own wallet the whole time.

Swapping back to SOL is usually instant, but the price depends on pool depth at that moment — this is not a savings account and there is no guaranteed exit price.

beforeBuy.p2: No shareholder rights come with them: no vote, and dividends only if the issuer chooses to pass them on. If the issuer fails, the token is worth whatever the market thinks their promise is worth.

swap.step4: Tap Review, then approve the token if this is your first time using it.
swap.step5: Confirm in your wallet and wait for the transaction to settle.

farm.step4: Stake the LP tokens to earn additional rewards.

signals.step2: Confidence shows how much those indicators agree — low confidence means the chart is unclear.

trade.title: Practice trading

trade.step2: Prices are real and live, so the practice is realistic.
trade.step3: Use it to learn order mechanics before risking anything on the Swap screen.

security.title: Staying safe
security.step1: Your seed phrase is the only backup. Written on paper, stored offline, never typed into a website.
security.step2: Enable biometric unlock and two-factor in Settings for device-level protection.
security.step3: Verify token contract addresses independently before swapping unknown tokens.
security.step4: Start with a small test transaction when using any new feature.
security.step5: Keep large holdings in a separate hardware wallet, not in an in-app wallet.
security.pitfall: Nobody legitimate will ever ask for your 12 recovery words. Not our support, not a group admin, not any website. Anyone who asks is trying to take your money. Block them immediately.

why.title: Why Fanous Bazaar Pishgam is different
why.sub: What we do that other apps don't
why.step1: Best-price routing: your swap is quoted across every DEX on the chain at once, not just one exchange. On a volatile pair that difference is often larger than any fee.
why.step2: Ten swap networks in one app — BNB Chain, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Avalanche, Linea, Sonic and Solana. Choose the network that holds your token before trading.
why.step3: Truly non-custodial: no signup, no KYC, no deposit address. Your funds never sit in our account, so there is no withdrawal queue and nothing to freeze.
why.step4: AI analysis built in, with honest confidence figures — it tells you when the signal is unclear instead of inventing certainty to look smart.
why.step5: One clear fee: {{fee}}% per swap, shown before you sign. No spread markup, no hidden withdrawal charge, no monthly cost.
why.pitfall: Compare the 'minimum received' figure, not the advertised rate. Some apps show a great headline rate then take a wide spread on top. Ours is the number you actually get.

strategy.title: Getting more out of the app
strategy.sub: Practical ways to grow what you have
strategy.step1: Start with a stablecoin pool. USDT/USDC pairs barely move against each other, so you collect trading fees with very little impermanent loss.
strategy.step2: Swap during high-volume hours. Deeper liquidity means less price impact, which matters far more on large trades than the fee does.
strategy.step3: Check the Signals screen before entering. If confidence is under 40% the chart genuinely isn't saying anything — waiting is a position too.
strategy.step4: Invite friends. Referrals are the fastest way up the leaderboard, and each new trader deepens the pools everyone uses.
strategy.step5: Keep gas money on each chain you use. Running out mid-transaction wastes the fee you already paid.
strategy.pitfall: Chasing the highest APR you can find is how most people lose money in DeFi. A steady 8% you understand beats a 900% pool whose token you can't sell.

audit.title: Security
audit.intro: What protects you, exactly how far each protection reaches, and what is not audited. Overstating any of this would make you less careful, which would cost you more than the reassurance is worth.
audit.nonCustodialBody: FBT Swap has no deposit address. There is no account with a balance, no wallet we control on your behalf, and no button anywhere in our systems that moves your funds. Every transaction is signed on your device by your own wallet. This is the foundation everything else on this page rests on.

keys.title: Your recovery phrase never leaves your device
keys.body: The 12-word phrase is generated on your phone using the operating system's own cryptographic random source, and it is never transmitted anywhere. Our servers have never seen one and are not built to receive one.
keys.limit: Which means we cannot recover it for you. If you lose the phrase and your device, the funds are gone permanently — not withheld, gone. Write it on paper.

encryption.title: Encrypted at rest with your password
encryption.body: The phrase is stored encrypted with AES-GCM, using a key stretched from your password by PBKDF2 with 310,000 iterations of SHA-256 — the OWASP-recommended figure. Someone who copies the stored file without your password gets ciphertext.
encryption.limit: The strength is your password's strength. 310,000 iterations makes each guess slow; it does not make a six-character password safe.

server.title: A server breach cannot take your funds
server.body: Our backend proxies market data, caches prices and forwards quotes. It holds no keys, no balances and no ability to sign anything. If it were fully compromised tomorrow, an attacker would gain a price cache.
server.limit: They could serve a wrong quote. Always check the amount your wallet shows you before signing — your wallet's number is the one that is binding, not ours.

lock.title: App lock and biometrics
lock.body: A PIN, TOTP two-factor or your device's fingerprint or face unlock can gate the app, and it auto-locks after inactivity. This genuinely protects you from someone who picks up your unlocked phone.
lock.limit: It gates this app's interface, nothing more. Anyone holding your recovery phrase can restore the wallet in any other app and spend from it, and our lock is irrelevant to them.

privacy.title: What we can see about you
privacy.body: No account, no email, no phone number, no identity check. The server sees the requests you make and the IP they come from, the same as any website. Your wallet address is sent when you ask for its balance, and it is not stored against a profile.
privacy.limit: The blockchain itself is public. Anyone who learns your address can read its entire history forever, from us or from anywhere else. That is a property of public blockchains, not of this app.

network.title: Where the app talks to
network.body: Fonts, icons and all app code are served from our own origin, so the app renders identically with no third-party requests. Price data, swap quotes and blockchain calls go to named providers over HTTPS only.
network.limit: External links — a P2P desk, a payment page, a podcast — open in a browser tab where the real domain stays visible, deliberately. Check that domain before typing anything into it.

audit.threatsIntro: In order of how often it happens. None of these are exotic attacks on cryptography — every one is somebody being persuaded to do something.

phrase.title: Giving away the recovery phrase
phrase.body: This is the overwhelming majority of losses. Nobody legitimate ever needs your 12 words: not support, not a giveaway, not a "wallet validation" page, not us. Anyone who asks is stealing from you, and there is no exception to that rule.

approvals.title: Signing an unlimited token approval
approvals.body: A malicious site asks you to approve a token and requests unlimited spending. Nothing happens that day. Weeks later the contract drains everything of that token. Approve only the amount you are trading, and revoke old approvals you no longer use.

fakeApps.title: A convincing fake of this app
fakeApps.body: Copies of wallet apps appear constantly on unofficial stores and in search ads. They look identical and send your phrase to somebody else. Install only from a link on our own site, and check the domain in the address bar before you download.

address.title: Sending to the wrong address or network
address.body: The same address string can exist on several networks, and a transfer sent on the wrong one is usually unrecoverable. Scan a QR code rather than typing, and if the amount is large, send a small test first.

support.title: Somebody pretending to be support
support.body: Fake helpers appear within minutes of any public complaint about a wallet. Real support never messages first, never asks for a phrase or a password, and never asks you to move funds to a "safe" address. Ours is one email address, listed on the Contact page.

dev.intro: A read-only market API, no key and no signup. Everything below is a real registered route on this server, checked rather than remembered — the previous version of this page advertised an endpoint that had been deleted, which is the one mistake documentation must not make.
dev.quickstartBody: No key, no account, no header beyond accept. Paste this and it works right now.
dev.rules: What you need to know first

base.v: {{base}}/api — the same origin the app itself uses. There is no separate developer host, so if the app is up, the API is up.

auth.v: None on any endpoint listed here. They are all public read-only data. If a request of ours ever asks you for a key, it is not ours.

limit.v: 120 requests per minute per IP across /api, and a separate, much tighter 10 per minute on the AI routes because each of those spends shared upstream quota. Over the limit you get HTTP 429 with a retry-after header in seconds — read it rather than guessing a backoff.

errors.v: Always JSON, never an HTML error page, always shaped {"error":"CODE"}. Upstream failures come back as 502 UPSTREAM_FAILED rather than a 200 with empty data, so you can tell "nothing happened" apart from "nothing exists".

cors.v: Open by default, so you can call this straight from a browser with no proxy of your own.

caching.v: Responses are cached server-side: market data for seconds, news and radio for 30 minutes, coin-id lookups for an hour. Polling faster than that spends your rate limit to receive the identical bytes.

step.s1: Agree the price and amount with the other person first — off the app. FBT Swap is not involved in that negotiation and cannot arbitrate it.
step.s2: Ask them for their receiving address AND the network it is on. The same address string can exist on several networks; sending on the wrong one usually loses the funds.
step.s3: Scan their QR code instead of typing. If you must type or paste, compare the first four and last four characters against the original before continuing.
step.s4: Send a small test amount first when the sum is large. Losing a dollar to a mistake is a lesson; losing the whole amount is not recoverable.
step.s5: Send the rest, then give them the transaction link so they can verify it on-chain themselves.

p2p.howTitle: How to buy with cash, step by step
p2p.howIntro: Every desk below works the same way. The escrow is what protects you, so the whole method is: never leave it, and never release before the money is genuinely in your account.

buyStep.b1: Open one of the desks below and create an account. You will need identity verification — that is not optional on any real desk, and a platform offering to skip it is the warning sign, not the bargain.
buyStep.b2: Choose BUY, pick your own currency, and sort by price. Ignore the very best rate and look at the seller's completed-order count and release time instead. A rate two percent worse from someone with 5,000 trades is the cheaper option once your time is counted.
buyStep.b3: Open the order for the amount you want. The moment you do, the desk LOCKS the seller's crypto in escrow. They cannot take it back, and this is the only thing standing between you and a stranger — which is why every instruction below is about not leaving it.
buyStep.b4: Pay using the exact method the order names, from an account in YOUR OWN name. Send the precise amount. Never write 'crypto', 'USDT' or the desk's name in the payment reference — banks freeze accounts over that wording.
buyStep.b5: Mark the order paid and upload your receipt. Then wait. The seller releases and the crypto lands in your desk account, usually in minutes.
buyStep.b6: Withdraw to your own wallet — do not leave it sitting on the desk. Copy your address from the Wallet screen, pick the SAME network on both sides, and send a small test amount first if the sum is large.

p2p.scamsIntro: Every one of these works by getting you outside the escrow, or by getting you to release before the money is really yours. If you recognise the shape, none of them work.
p2p.cashTitle: Buying with physical cash, in person
p2p.cashBody: Meeting someone with banknotes has no escrow at all — nothing can be reversed and nobody can arbitrate. If you do it anyway: meet inside a bank branch or a police-station lobby in daylight, count the notes before touching your phone, and have the sender broadcast the transaction while you are both standing there. Never travel to a private address, and never hand over cash against a screenshot — only against a confirmation you have read on-chain yourself.

swap.title: 1 · Swap — exchanging tokens
swap.lead: A swap converts one token directly into another with no deposit to any exchange. Tokens leave your own wallet and the new token arrives in your own wallet in the same transaction.
swap.s1body: At the top of the Swap screen you choose the network (BNB, Ethereum, Polygon…). Tokens only exist on the network they were issued on. If your USDT is on BNB Chain, set the network to BNB Chain.
swap.s2title: Choose two tokens and an amount
swap.s2body: The top box is what you pay, the bottom box is what you receive. As soon as you type an amount, the app searches several decentralised exchanges for the best route and shows what you would get.
swap.s3body: Three numbers matter: the rate, the price impact, and the minimum received. A price impact above 2% means that pair is thin and you are overpaying — reduce the amount or pick a different pair.
swap.s4body: The first time you trade a given token, you must send an approval transaction so the contract may move it. It costs network gas but is needed only once per token. The network's own coin (e.g. BNB) never needs approval.
swap.s5title: Swap, then sign in your wallet
swap.s5body: Your wallet opens and shows the details. Sign there. A few seconds later the transaction is on-chain and you get a link to it.
swap.feeTitle: There are two fees — both real
swap.feeBody: 1) Network gas: charged by the blockchain, not by us. You must hold some of the network's own coin or the transaction is rejected. 2) The Fanous Bazaar Pishgam platform fee: {{fee}}% of every swap, paid to the company wallet in the same transaction. It is our revenue and it is shown to you before you sign.
swap.slipBody: The price moves between the moment you tap and the moment the transaction is mined. Slippage is the worst price you are willing to accept. 0.5% is fine for liquid tokens. Small tokens may need more, but the higher you set it, the worse the price you can end up with.
swap.failBody: Three common causes: not enough gas (top up the network's coin), slippage too tight for a moving price, or you skipped the approval. A failed transaction does not take your tokens, but the gas it burned is not refunded.

predict.title: 2 · Predictions and signals
predict.lead: This section helps you read the market. None of it is investment advice, and nobody knows the future.
predict.s1body: On the Predict screen you guess whether a coin goes up or down. Wins and losses are in points, which exist only for ranking and fun and have no monetary value. Nothing is taken from you and nothing is paid out.
predict.s2body: Every signal has three parts: a price range (never a single exact number), an invalidation level at which the idea is wrong, and a confidence score. Anywhere you see a guaranteed number, you are being scammed — we never publish one.
predict.s3body: RSI above 70 suggests heavy buying, below 30 heavy selling. MACD shows the direction of momentum. These are aids only; markets can move against an indicator for a long time.
predict.s4body: Never put in money you need. Crypto has dropped 30% in a single day many times. If your thesis is wrong, taking a small loss beats waiting and hoping.

wallet.title: 3 · Connecting a wallet on mobile
wallet.lead: Fanous Bazaar Pishgam never holds your assets and has no deposit address. To trade you connect your own wallet. There are three ways.
wallet.m1title: Option 1 — the wallet's built-in browser (easiest on a phone)
wallet.m1body: Open MetaMask or Trust Wallet, tap Browser in the bottom menu, and enter the Fanous Bazaar Pishgam address there. The wallet is detected automatically and connecting is one tap. Try this first if connecting gives you trouble.
wallet.m2body: Tap connect and choose WalletConnect. On mobile you get a list of installed wallets; tap yours, it opens directly, approve, then use the back gesture to return to Fanous Bazaar Pishgam.
wallet.m3title: Option 3 — the built-in Fanous Bazaar Pishgam wallet
wallet.m3body: If you have no wallet at all, the app can create one here. Its key is encrypted on your own device with your password and is never transmitted. Write the recovery phrase down on paper.
wallet.p1title: Problem: I tap connect and nothing happens
wallet.p1body: A normal mobile browser (Chrome, Safari) has no wallet inside it. Either use WalletConnect, or open the site inside your wallet's own browser.
wallet.p2title: Problem: I approve in the wallet but come back disconnected
wallet.p2body: Common on Android: the system kills the backgrounded app and the session drops. Turn battery optimisation off for both Fanous Bazaar Pishgam and your wallet, and return with the back gesture rather than closing the app.
wallet.p3title: Problem: connected but the balance shows zero
wallet.p3body: Almost always the wrong network. Your USDT may be on TRON while Fanous Bazaar Pishgam is looking at BNB Chain. Switch network at the top of the Swap screen. Balances on TRON or Bitcoin are not supported by on-chain swaps here.
wallet.p4title: Problem: the wallet says unknown network
wallet.p4body: Your wallet hasn't added that chain yet. Fanous Bazaar Pishgam offers to add it when you swap — tap Approve / Switch network. It is harmless and only adds a network entry to your wallet.
wallet.p5title: Problem: the transaction is stuck pending
wallet.p5body: You underpaid gas while the network was busy. Use Speed up or Cancel in your wallet. Until it settles, the next transaction from that wallet is stuck behind it.
wallet.p6body: Some wallet and node services are restricted on certain networks. If prices stay blank or a connection hangs, switch between mobile data and Wi-Fi and try again.
wallet.p7title: Problem: MetaMask opens but says the URL is invalid
wallet.p7body: This was a bug in older builds: the app sent 'https://localhost' as its identity, which means nothing to a wallet running as a separate app. Update to the latest version. If it still happens, use the wallet's own browser instead (Option 1).
wallet.p8title: Tip: scan instead of typing an address
wallet.p8body: Wherever an address is needed, use the scan button rather than typing. An address is 42 characters with no checksum you can read by eye, transfers are irreversible, and one wrong character sends the money nowhere. If your device cannot scan, paste it and then check the first four and last four characters against the original.

security.title: 4 · Security — the part that matters most
security.lead: In crypto, stolen money does not come back. There is no bank to complain to and no transaction to reverse. Take these rules seriously.
security.s1title: Your recovery phrase is your money
security.s1body: The 12 or 24 words you get when creating a wallet are the money itself. Anyone holding them takes everything, with no password needed. Write them on paper and store it safely.
security.s2body: Don't screenshot the phrase, don't message it to yourself on Telegram or WhatsApp, don't keep it in cloud notes, and never type it into a website or form. Photo galleries and messengers both sync to the cloud.
security.s3title: Fanous Bazaar Pishgam will never ask for your recovery phrase
security.s3body: Not in the app, not in support, not in any message. Anyone asking for it in our name is a scammer, even with our logo and name on their profile.
security.s4body: In Settings enable biometrics and two-factor, and set auto-lock to a few minutes. If you lose the phone, that is the only thing standing between a thief and your built-in wallet.
security.s5title: Back up — and know what isn't a backup
security.s5body: The Fanous Bazaar Pishgam backup file is the same encrypted blob; without your password it is useless, so forgetting the password makes the file worthless too. Paper is the real backup, not the file. Uninstalling without paper destroys the built-in wallet permanently.
security.s6body: Read every wallet prompt: which token, how much, to which address. If anything differs from what Fanous Bazaar Pishgam showed you, close it and do not sign.
security.s7body: Some sites ask for unlimited approval. If your wallet allows it, cap the amount at exactly this trade. Periodically clear old approvals with a revoke tool.
security.s8body: A free airdrop that first needs your wallet connected; an unknown token that appeared by itself and cannot be sold; fake support in Telegram that replies first; and thousand-percent yields. All four want the same thing: your signature.

buy.title: Buy & sell

buy.heading: Turning money into crypto
buy.body: FBT does not sell crypto and never holds your money — there is no deposit address here and never will be. What this page does is point you at the routes that work, so the coins arrive directly in a wallet only you control.

sell.heading: Turning crypto back into money
sell.body: Same principle in reverse. You send crypto from your own wallet to a buyer or a desk, and they pay you. FBT never takes custody at any point, which is why we cannot reverse a transfer or recover one sent to the wrong place. Check the address and the network twice before you send.

p2p.name: Person to person (P2P)
p2p.buy: Buy from another person through a desk that holds the crypto in escrow until you have paid.
p2p.sell: Sell to another person with the same escrow protection. Usually the best rate.

receive.name: Receive from someone you know
receive.buy: The simplest route: show your address and have them send. No third party, no fee, no rate.
receive.sell: Send directly to their address. Confirm the network first — a wrong network loses the funds.

swap.name: Already hold crypto?
swap.buy: Then skip the fiat step. Swap what you have for what you want, right here.
swap.sell: Convert to a stablecoin first, then cash out. Often smoother than selling a volatile coin.

bisq.name: Bisq — peer-to-peer, no account
bisq.buy: Open-source desktop software. No registration and no identity check: you buy directly from another person and the bitcoin sits in 2-of-2 multisig, so nobody — including Bisq — can take it. Desktop only, which is its one real drawback.
bisq.sell: Sell directly to another person over Tor, with no account and no verification. The bitcoin stays in multisig escrow until you confirm the money arrived. Desktop only.

hodlhodl.name: Hodl Hodl — peer-to-peer, works on a phone
hodlhodl.buy: Non-custodial escrow, no verification required, 100+ currencies, running since 2018. It needs an email address, but unlike Bisq it works in a mobile browser. Bitcoin only.
hodlhodl.sell: Sell bitcoin to a person of your choosing with multisig escrow protecting both sides. No identity check, and it works on a phone. Bitcoin only.

buy.addressHint: This is your own address on {{chain}}. Anyone sending you crypto must use this exact address AND this network. A wrong network means the funds are gone — nobody can recover them.
buy.connectFirst: Connect a wallet first, so you have an address for the coins to arrive at.

warn.network: The network must match. The same address exists on BNB Chain, Ethereum and Polygon; sending on the wrong one is permanent.
warn.reversal: Bank transfers can be reversed by the sender for weeks afterwards. Crypto transfers cannot. Never release crypto before the money has truly settled.
warn.escrow: Only trade where an escrow holds the crypto. If someone asks you to move the deal off-platform, that is the scam.
warn.rate: Compare the rate against the market price on the Market tab. A rate far better than everyone else's is bait.

buy.notAdvice: Nothing here is financial advice, and we do not endorse any desk or counterparty. You are dealing with third parties at your own risk. Crypto transactions are irreversible.

verdict.title: The full picture
verdict.subtitle: Four independent readings — the chart, this asset's own track record, its structure, and the market it lives in. They are allowed to disagree, and when they do we say so.

stanceExplain.tailwind: Every layer we can measure currently leans the same way, upward. That is not a promise — it means the conditions that have historically preceded gains are present right now.
stanceExplain.mildUp: The balance leans up, but weakly. A single piece of news is enough to erase an edge this small.
stanceExplain.unclear: The honest answer. Either the readings contradict each other or there is not enough history to say anything. Most of the time, for most assets, this is the correct answer — and it is the one that saves money.
stanceExplain.mildDown: The balance leans down, but weakly. Not a reason to panic; a reason not to add.
stanceExplain.headwind: Every layer we can measure currently leans the same way, downward. Assets do rise in these conditions — they just do it less often.

agree.aligned: Both horizons point the same way. That is the strongest form this read ever takes.
agree.conflict: The week and the month disagree. Usually this means a short-term move is running against the bigger picture — the sort of thing that reverses.
agree.partial: One horizon has an opinion and the other does not. Treat the unclear one as unclear, not as agreement.

regime.riskOn: Money is flowing into the market as a whole and spreading beyond Bitcoin. Historically that is when everything else gets its turn.
regime.btcLed: The market is rising but Bitcoin is taking most of it. Altcoins often lag badly in this phase.
regime.rotationOut: The market is falling and money is moving into Bitcoin. This is the phase where altcoins are sold first and hardest — no chart of theirs shows it coming.
regime.riskOff: Money is leaving the market broadly, Bitcoin included. Almost everything falls together in this phase, regardless of how good its own chart looks.

beta.high: This asset historically moves about {{beta}}× as hard as Bitcoin. A 10% Bitcoin day has meant roughly {{tenPct}}% here, in both directions. ({{r2}}% of its movement is explained by Bitcoin.)
beta.normal: This asset moves roughly in line with Bitcoin ({{beta}}×).
beta.low: This asset has moved less than Bitcoin ({{beta}}×) — it has been the quieter side of the market.

cycle.farFromHigh: {{drop}}% below its all-time high. A {{recoveryX}}× rise just to break even. Most assets this far down never return.

plain.title: In plain words
plain.tailwind: All four readings currently point the same way. That is a description of present conditions, not a forecast: historically, when this combination has appeared, the following period was more often up than down. Often is not always.
plain.mildUp: The balance leans slightly positive. The margin is small enough that a single piece of news would erase it, so it is not something to build a position around on its own.
plain.unclear: There is no clear signal here, and that is the accurate answer rather than a missing one. The readings contradict each other or there is too little history to measure. This is the most common outcome for most assets on most days.
plain.mildDown: The balance leans slightly negative. That is an argument for waiting rather than for selling — a small edge in either direction is not a reason to act.
plain.headwind: All four readings currently point the same way, downward. Assets still rise in these conditions; historically they have simply done so less often from this starting point.

verdict.notPrediction: This is not a prediction and there is no price target anywhere in it. Every number above is measured from what already happened: this asset's own history, its relationship with Bitcoin, and the state of the market. The future is allowed to ignore all of it. Never put in money you cannot afford to lose.

bridge.title: Bridge
bridge.subtitle: Move stablecoins between networks without leaving the app.
bridge.whatBody: Your USDT on BNB Chain and USDT on Arbitrum are different tokens on different networks — you cannot send one to the other directly. A bridge locks the first and releases the second. We route through LI.FI, which compares every bridge and picks the cheapest, and your wallet signs it. We never hold your funds at any point.
bridge.connectFirst: Connect a wallet to get a quote.
bridge.sentBody: The transaction is on-chain. Bridges take anywhere from seconds to several minutes — the funds will appear on the destination network when the relayer completes it. You can close this screen.
bridge.riskBody: A bridge is two transactions on two networks with a relayer in between. If the relayer is slow, funds can sit in transit for a while — this is normal and they are not lost. Keep a little of the destination network's gas coin so you can move the funds once they arrive. Bridges have also been the target of the largest hacks in crypto; only bridge what you are willing to have in transit.
bridge.disclaimer: We are an interface. The transfer is executed by LI.FI and the underlying bridge, not by Fanous Bazaar Pishgam — we never take custody and cannot reverse, cancel or recover a transfer. Our {{fee}} share is shown in the quote before you sign.

bridge.slippageNote: Slippage tolerance is {{pct}}%, taken from your Settings so it matches the swap screen. Raise it only if quotes keep failing — a bridge takes minutes and cannot be cheaply retried, so a loose tolerance costs more here than it does on a swap.

bridge.betterRoute: {{name}} leaves you about {{amount}} more after every fee, including the fixed one.

restrict.title: Where this works
restrict.intro: Nothing we built is restricted. The swap, the wallet, market data, charts and orders are non-custodial: no account, no identity check, no country blocked, and no permission needed from anyone — including us. This page is only about the third parties we link out to, because the exchanges and payment providers publish their own country lists and we would rather you knew before you signed up anywhere.

eu.name: European Union
eu.note: Card and SEPA bank transfer both work. EUR purchases start at about €16.50, which is the lowest minimum of any currency here.

uk.name: United Kingdom
uk.note: Card payments in GBP work. Some crypto exchanges apply extra FCA-driven checks on first use, so expect an identity step.

turkey.name: Türkiye
turkey.note: TRY card payments work, and all three P2P desks list Turkish lira. Minimums are higher in lira terms — around ₺906 — simply because of the exchange rate.

uae.name: United Arab Emirates
uae.note: AED card payments work. Minimum around 70 AED.

global.name: Most other countries
global.note: Usually fine with a card issued locally. The payment provider decides at checkout based on where the card was issued, not on where you happen to be sitting.

us.name: United States
us.note: ChangeNOW’s own terms exclude US residents from their service. The P2P desks also restrict or bar US users. This is their rule, not ours.

iran.name: Iran
iran.note: Binance, OKX and Bybit all publish Iran as fully blocked under OFAC sanctions, and ChangeNOW’s terms exclude sanctioned jurisdictions. Signing up by giving another country as your residence risks the account being frozen after you have deposited — which is materially worse than never opening one. The swap, the wallet and everything else in this app work normally and need no account anywhere.

restrict.cards: One thing no provider can waive: Visa, Mastercard and Amex have been disconnected from Iran’s banking system at the network level since 2012. An Iranian bank card cannot authorise a foreign crypto purchase. That is the payment networks themselves, not a company policy.
restrict.ourPosition: None of this applies to the parts of FBT Swap that are ours. The swap, the wallet, market data, charts and orders are non-custodial and need no account, no identity check and no permission from anyone. These restrictions only concern the third parties we link out to.
restrict.sourceNote: Taken from each provider’s own published terms and country lists, checked rather than assumed. If one of them changes its policy, this page is wrong until we update it — check the provider before you rely on it.

vault.title: FBT Lending Vault
vault.body: Deposit a stablecoin and it is lent to over-collateralised borrowers on Morpho. You keep the yield, you can withdraw at any time, and we never hold your funds — the vault is a smart contract you can read.
vault.risk: We decide which lending markets this vault uses, and that is a real risk you are taking on us. Lending markets can take bad debt and smart contracts can be exploited. Our fee is a share of the yield only — if the vault earns nothing, we earn nothing.
vault.venueNote: Deposits and withdrawals happen on Morpho’s own audited interface, not inside this app, so you never depend on us being online to reach your money.

hardware.title: Keep your keys where this app cannot reach them
hardware.intro: Your keys live on this phone. That is fine for everyday amounts and it is how a non-custodial wallet works — but a phone gets lost, stolen, and reads messages from strangers. A hardware wallet keeps the key on a separate device that never connects to the internet, so a compromised phone cannot spend your funds. You still swap here; you just sign with something a thief has to physically hold.
hardware.ledgerBlurb: Nano, Flex and Stax. The most widely supported devices — works with almost every wallet app.
hardware.trezorBlurb: Open-source firmware you can read and verify yourself, rather than trust.
hardware.disclosure: If you buy through this link we receive {{rate}}% of the sale from {{vendor}}. It costs you nothing extra, and we would recommend a hardware wallet with or without it.
hardware.cautionTitle: Never buy one second-hand, and why that matters more than the brand
hardware.caution: Buy only from the manufacturer or an official reseller. A marketplace, second-hand or gifted device can be tampered with, and one that arrives with a recovery phrase already printed is a theft in progress — a real device makes you generate it yourself, offline, on first use.
hardware.notRequired: None of this is required to use FBT Swap. Everything here works with the wallet you already have — this is for people holding an amount they would be genuinely sorry to lose.

calm.title: Calm music
calm.whyTitle: Why music is on a trading screen
calm.why1: Calm in investing. A clearer head makes a better decision — and in markets that is not a nice sentiment, it is the whole difference between a plan and a reaction.
calm.why2: The two most expensive habits in trading are selling in a panic and buying out of frustration. Neither is a mistake of analysis; both are what happens when you decide while your pulse is up. If a few minutes of quiet stops one impulsive trade, this tab has paid for itself many times over.
calm.why3: So this is not entertainment. Put it on before you open a position, not instead of reading the chart. Nothing here is advice, and music will not tell you what a market is going to do.
calm.credit: Every track is Public Domain, CC BY or CC BY-SA — freely reusable, with the artist named on each row as the licence requires. Streamed from the Internet Archive's own servers; we host nothing and change nothing.

thor.whatTitle: What a native swap is, and how it differs from bridging
thor.what1: This swaps REAL Bitcoin for REAL Ethereum. Not wrapped BTC, not a token that represents Bitcoin somewhere else — actual coins settled on their own chains by THORChain, a network with no company behind it and no account to open.
thor.what2: It is not the same as the Tokens tab. That one moves ERC-20 tokens between EVM chains and your wallet signs it. Here you send coins yourself, from whatever wallet holds them, to an address the network gives you.
thor.what3: We show you the price, the address and the exact memo. We deliberately do not send it for you: we hold no Bitcoin keys and never will, and a swap like this is completed by your own wallet.
thor.destinationPlaceholder: The address that should receive the coins
thor.destinationNote: Check this address character by character. It is where the coins land, it must be on the receiving chain, and nobody — not us, not THORChain — can reverse a transfer to the wrong place.
thor.sendWarning: Send only the asset you selected, only to this address, and only before the quote expires. This address changes between quotes — never reuse an old one.
thor.memoWarning: The memo is the instruction. Paste it exactly, with no spaces added and nothing missing. A wallet that cannot attach a memo cannot be used for this, and a swap sent without one — or with a broken one — cannot be recovered by anyone.
thor.noFeeNote: We earn nothing on this particular swap. Bitcoin-family chains cap the memo at 80 bytes and our fee identifier does not fit, so the fee is left off rather than the swap being refused. You pay less; we simply do not take a cut here.

tron.badAddress: That is not a Tron address. It should start with T and be 34 characters. An Ethereum 0x address will not work here.
tron.tooSmall: Tron charges a roughly fixed cost to receive, so small transfers lose a large share of their value. Below about ${{min}} this is rarely worth it — the same fee is barely noticeable on a larger amount.
tron.severeLoss: You lose {{pct}}% of this transfer. Almost all of that is Tron's fixed receiving cost, not our fee — sending a larger amount at once costs the same in absolute terms.
tron.sentBody: Sent. The bridge delivers USDT to your Tron address, usually within a couple of minutes. Check your Tron wallet, not this screen.
tron.whyTitle: Why send to Tron at all?
tron.whyBody: USDT on Tron is the cheapest widely-accepted way to hold and move dollars — sending it later costs cents. The catch is getting it there: the receiving side has a near-fixed cost, so it pays to move a meaningful amount once rather than small amounts often. We take 0.30% on this route, shown in the quote before you sign.

perks.title: What your rank unlocks
perks.intro: Each rank unlocks a real discount on a venue we work with. Nothing here is a voucher we invented — the discount is the venue's own referral benefit, and it applies the moment you use the code.
perks.howTitle: Why does this cost me nothing?
perks.howBody: Because the venue pays us, not you. Trade through our code and they give you a lower fee than you would get going there directly — then pay us a slice of what they keep. You are not funding this discount; they are, because bringing them a trader is worth more to them than the few basis points they give up. Your points stay exactly where they are. A rank is something you reach and keep, not a balance that drains every time you use it.

board.title: Local board
board.safetyTitle: Nobody is holding the money — not even us
board.safetyBody: This is a notice board, not an exchange. We do not hold anyone’s funds, we cannot reverse a payment, and we cannot settle an argument between two people. Anything you agree here you agree directly with a stranger. Meet in daylight in a public place, count cash before you touch your phone, and never release crypto for a screenshot — only for a confirmation you have read on the chain yourself.
board.connectFirst: Connect a wallet to post. Your wallet address is your identity here — there is no signup and no password.
board.empty: No adverts yet. Yours would be the first.
board.offline: The board is unreachable right now. Try again in a moment.
board.proNote: Paid in {{symbol}} on {{chain}}, straight from your wallet to ours. We check the transaction on the chain before the placement starts, so nothing is taken on trust. Network gas is separate and goes to {{chain}}, not to us.
board.footerNotice: Adverts are written by users. We do not verify them, we take no part in the trade, and we hold no money at any point. The only thing we charge for on this screen is the listing slot ({{prices}}).
board.costsBody: Paid in {{symbol}} on {{chain}}, straight from your wallet to ours. Your advert stays hidden until the payment is confirmed on the chain — we check it ourselves, so nothing is taken on trust. Network gas is separate and goes to {{chain}}, not to us.
board.costsRefund: There is a charge because a free board fills up with adverts from people who have nothing to sell. Paying keeps it worth reading. Payments are final and cannot be refunded, so check your text before you pay.
board.draftHidden: Saved, but nobody can see it yet. Choose how long you want it live.
board.liveUntil: Live until {{date}}. Paying again adds to the time you have left.

community.title: Community feed
community.intro: Live posts from Farcaster, an open social protocol. Reading is free and needs no account. These are not our posts and this is not our network — we only show it.

community.joinBody: You need a Farcaster account, which costs a few dollars a year in storage rent paid to the protocol — not to us. We deliberately cannot post on your behalf: that would mean holding your signing key, and we do not hold keys of any kind.
community.notice: These posts are written by strangers on a public network. We do not host them, verify them or moderate them, and showing a post is not a recommendation. Never send anyone money or a recovery phrase because of something you read here.

limits.title: Before you buy — where this works
limits.l1: Countries: 233 supported. Iran, Syria, Cuba and North Korea are not among them and the catalogue stays empty there. Turkey, the UAE, Iraq, Lebanon, Russia, Europe and Asia all work.
limits.l2: Region lock: most cards only redeem in the country they were bought for. A VPN does not get around it and can flag the account.
limits.l3: Refunds: an unused code can usually be exchanged. A code redeemed in the wrong region cannot.
limits.l4: Delivery: by email, within minutes. Give an address you can actually open.
limits.l5: Payment: USDC, USDT and 15+ coins on Solana, Base, Tron, Polygon and more. Cryptorefills is the merchant — your money never passes through us.

fbt.title: Your FBT balance
fbt.notCoin: FBT is a loyalty balance inside this app. It is not a tradable coin, has no price, and cannot be sold or withdrawn — it buys you lower fees and free adverts here.

how.h1: You earn FBT for using the app: swapping, inviting a friend, checking in. Nothing is bought and nothing is sold.
how.h2: Fee discounts are shown here and go live with the next swap update; adverts already work.
how.h3: From Silver it also pays for adverts on the board, which otherwise cost $1 to $25.
how.h4: If we ever issue a real on-chain token, this balance converts one-to-one. Until then it stays here, and we do not promise a date or a value.

ostium.risk: These are leveraged perpetual derivatives, not the underlying gold, oil or shares. Leverage can liquidate all your collateral. Most retail leveraged traders lose money.
ostium.nonCustodialTitle: Your wallet signs; FBT never holds your funds
ostium.nonCustodialBody: Ostium's audited contracts lock USDC on Arbitrum. The transaction includes our disclosed builder fee and is signed directly by your wallet.

ostium.rolloverNotice: Ostium also charges variable rollover costs while a position remains open. They are not included in the one-time opening-cost total above.
